title: The cluster size distribution of a stationary discrete random field is the normalized weight sequence of its clusters
author: Dan Cheng and John Ginos
work: Cluster size distributions of discrete random fields
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Theorem 2.2 of the article (source label thm:CSD_d, source0.tex lines 418--429), the cluster size distribution formula that is the main theoretical result of the paper: for a stationary random field and a threshold $u$ satisfying the finite-cluster assumption with $\rho_u=\P(R_u(o))>0$, the probability that the cluster at the origin has size $k$ equals $w_k/\rho_u$, where $w_k$ is the weight defined by the paper's earlier formula. It is delivered with the authors' own complete 27-line proof at source0.tex lines 431--457. H2: the proof is a genuine decomposition argument for dependent spatial data rather than a qualifying examination exercise. The solver must use stationarity to move the cluster root to the origin, decompose the event that the cluster size equals $k$ into the disjoint events indexed by the possible cluster shapes containing the origin, identify the probability of each shape with the corresponding weight $w_k$ through the finite-cluster structure, and then sum the disjoint contributions and normalize by $\rho_u$, which also requires the identity $\rho_u=\sum_{j\geq1}w_j$ that the statement records. Reproducing that cluster decomposition with its normalization is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying level.
